items.title: Thanksgiving nor'easter batters US East Coast
items.feedTitle: Thanksgiving Day storm batters Jersey Shore, Philadelphia area with strong winds, heavy rain
items.summary: A powerful coastal storm swept across the eastern United States on Thanksgiving, bringing heavy rain, strong winds, and significant flooding. By Thursday evening, more than 900,000 customers lost power across at least eight states from Maine to Florida. The storm disrupted holiday travel plans for millions, with flight delays and cancellations reported at major airports.

items.title: Zelensky compares Trump's Putin friendship to Hitler appeasement
items.feedTitle: Zelensky on Trump calling Putin 'friend': 'Same as somebody saying about Hitler' in WWII
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky responded critically to President Trump's description of Russian President Vladimir Putin as a 'friend,' calling the comparison similar to someone befriending Hitler during World War II. Zelensky also told the BBC that the US is too focused on the Middle East and not pushing Russia hard enough on Ukraine.

items.title: Trump claims Iran war ends 'whenever I want it
items.feedTitle: Trump: Iran war will be over 'sort of whenever I want it to be'
items.summary: President Trump told soldiers at Mar-a-Lago on Thanksgiving that the Iran war would be over 'sort of whenever I want it to be,' as the conflict stretches into its ninth month. Trump downplayed reports of Russian and Chinese support for Iran, saying the US does not need Middle East oil.

items.title: Man shot dead after Thanksgiving high school football game
items.feedTitle: Witness describes chaotic shooting after football game at Chelsea High School
items.summary: A shooting incident occurred on the sidelines of a Thanksgiving high school football game in Chelsea, Massachusetts, resulting in one fatality. Authorities are investigating the circumstances of the shooting, which occurred during what witnesses described as chaotic scenes after the game.

items.title: EPA reports zero airborne lead after Iowa detonation
items.feedTitle: News Wrap: EPA reports 'zero' airborne lead in Iowa
items.summary: The EPA announced that air monitors detected no airborne lead following the Army's controlled detonation of nearly five tons of lead azide explosive stockpile in Middletown, Iowa. The agency is awaiting laboratory results from environmental samples taken after the Thursday detonation.

stlouis.title: St. Louis records second-snowiest Thanksgiving in history
stlouis.feedTitle: This Thanksgiving is St. Louis’ second snowiest on record, National Weather Service says
stlouis.summary: St. Louis was blanketed with significant snowfall on Thanksgiving, marking the region's second-snowiest Thanksgiving on record according to the National Weather Service. The heavy, wet snow brought down trees and power lines across the metro area.

stlouis.title: 125,000 St. Louis homes remain without power after snowstorm
stlouis.feedTitle: Lost power on Thanksgiving? What to know as 125,000 homes in St. Louis region wait for crews
stlouis.summary: Nearly 125,000 homes in the St. Louis region and metro-east lost power after the Thanksgiving winter storm dumped heavy wet snow. Ameren crews warned that restoration could take days as they worked through widespread outages affecting multiple counties.

stlouis.title: Missouri Supreme Court disbar ex-Circuit Attorney Kim Gardner
stlouis.feedTitle: Missouri Supreme Court disbars ex-St. Louis Circuit Attorney Kim Gardner
stlouis.summary: The Missouri Supreme Court voted to disbar former St. Louis Circuit Attorney Kim Gardner, citing professional misconduct. Gardner, who served as the top prosecutor in the city, faces permanent revocation of her law license.

items.title: Two Italian technicians killed in Iran drone strike on Kuwait
items.feedTitle: Middle East latest: Two Italians killed in Iranian drone attack in Kuwait
items.summary: Two Italian nationals working as technicians for German defense company Rheinmetall were killed in an apparent Iranian drone strike on a Kuwaiti defense installation. Iran has denied responsibility, calling the incident 'suspicious,' but the attack has drawn global condemnation and heightened Middle East tensions.

items.title: New Zealand election: ruling coalition needs minor party support
items.feedTitle: New Zealand election: final results show ruling coalition needs minor party to govern
items.summary: Final results from New Zealand's general election show the incumbent right-leaning coalition led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon has fallen short of the parliamentary majority needed to govern alone. The coalition will require support from the centrist Opportunity party or face another election.

items.title: Zelensky tells BBC US too focused on Middle East
items.feedTitle: US too focused on Middle East and not pushing Russia hard enough, Zelensky tells BBC
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky criticized US foreign policy during a BBC interview, arguing that Washington is too focused on the Middle East and not pushing Russia hard enough on the Ukraine conflict. He also expressed concern about Trump's characterization of Putin as a friend.

items.title: UK shields fighter jets, mobilizes reservists amid Russia threat
items.feedTitle: UK shields fighter jets, contacts reservists in Cold War-scale push amid Russia threat
items.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence is taking Cold War-scale precautions, shielding fighter jets and contacting military reservists about potential mobilization as tensions with Russia escalate. Officials say the 'threat environment' has risen significantly in recent months.

items.title: UK net migration falls to 1997 lows excluding pandemic years
items.feedTitle: Net migration to UK falls to lowest level since 1997 excluding pandemic
items.summary: Net migration to the United Kingdom has fallen to its lowest level since 1997 when excluding pandemic years, with the difference between arrivals and departures reaching just 77,000 for the year to June. The sharp decline is attributed to both Labour government policies and broader economic factors beyond ministerial control.

items.title: Bangladesh considers ICJ move for Sheikh Hasina extradition
items.feedTitle: Bangladesh considers moving ICJ for Sheikh Hasina's extradition from India: Report | World News
items.summary: Bangladesh is reportedly considering approaching the International Court of Justice to seek the extradition of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who is currently in India. Hasina faces death sentence charges in absentia following the political upheaval in Bangladesh, and her planned December return has put New Delhi in a diplomatic bind.

items.title: India's GenAI course enrollments double in 2026
items.feedTitle: India's GenAI course enrollments double in 2026 to 12 per min, says report
items.summary: India has seen GenAI course enrollments double in 2026, with 12 students enrolling per minute on average, according to a new report. The surge reflects growing demand for artificial intelligence skills in India's job market.

items.title: 164 foreigners rescued from cyber fraud hub in Noida
items.feedTitle: 164 foreigners lured to India, held captive and forced into online investment fraud
items.summary: Delhi police busted an international human trafficking and cyber fraud operation in Noida that held 164 foreign nationals captive. The victims were promised legitimate jobs but were forced to participate in online investment scams and had their passports confiscated.

items.title: Two Jharkhand brothers arrested for murdering wives
items.feedTitle: Angry By Fights Between Their Wives, 2 Jharkhand Brothers Kill Them, Bury Bodies
items.summary: Police in Jharkhand arrested two brothers for the murder of their wives, whom they had reportedly grown angry with over frequent domestic fights. The brothers killed the women and buried their bodies in Simdega district.

items.title: Akhilesh Yadav On Stage, Azam Khan Says 'Wish He Spent 6 Months In Jail'

immigration.title: IBM ends H-1B sponsorship, sets December 31 exit deadline
immigration.feedTitle:
IBM stops sponsoring work visas
for most consulting roles in the US - The New Indian Express
immigration.summary: IBM announced it is discontinuing H-1B visa and green card sponsorship for most consulting roles and has told affected employees they must either relocate outside the US or leave the company by December 31, 2026. The move affects hundreds of Indian workers and marks a significant shift in the tech industry's approach to work-visa sponsorship.

immigration.title: Department of Labor proposes major PERM green card overhaul
immigration.feedTitle: US Labor Department Revises PERM Form for Green Card Sponsorship
immigration.summary: The US Department of Labor has proposed sweeping changes to the PERM (Permanent Employment-based Immigrant Visa) labor certification program, including 90-day recruitment periods and a 2-year layoff bar for employers filing green card petitions. The proposed rule, not yet finalized, would significantly tighten the process for employer-sponsored green cards.

immigration.title: H-1B visa appointment delays strand skilled workers abroad
immigration.feedTitle: H-1B visa delays leave skilled workers stranded abroad, says US Congressman
immigration.summary: US Congressman Ro Khanna highlighted that H-1B visa appointment delays are leaving skilled workers stranded outside the United States. The delays are attributed to staffing shortages at USCIS and State Department consulates processing visa applications.

items.title: Nifty 50 may hit 29,000 by end of 2027 on capex boom
items.feedTitle: Nifty 50 seen hitting 29,000 by 2027-end as JP Morgan spots broad private capex boom
items.summary: JP Morgan has identified a broad private capital expenditure boom that could propel the Nifty 50 index to 29,000 by the end of 2027. The forecast reflects optimism about India's economic growth trajectory, though the market is currently experiencing profit-booking near 26,000 levels.

items.title: Brent crude near monthly high as Middle East tensions fuel jitters
items.feedTitle: Brent Crude Near Month's High as Mideast Conflict Threatens Supply
items.summary: Brent crude oil prices have climbed near monthly highs as tensions in the Middle East, including the attack on Saudi refineries and Iranian drone strikes, threaten global oil supply. Market volatility reflects concerns over potential disruptions to energy production in the region.

items.title: Nvidia halts sales to Southeast Asia amid US export restrictions
items.feedTitle: Nvidia Tells Partners to Pause Shipments to Southeast Asia
items.summary: Nvidia has told partners to pause shipments of its most advanced AI chips to Southeast Asia as the US tightens restrictions on chip exports to China and Chinese-controlled entities. The move reflects escalating trade tensions and US efforts to maintain technological superiority.

items.title: China reserves right to respond to Trump's new tariff proposals
items.feedTitle: China reserves right to take ‘necessary measures’ after Trump’s new tariff proposals
items.summary: Beijing said it reserves the right to take 'necessary measures' after President Trump proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners including China and the EU. Trump's proposals amount to 'political manipulation,' China said, while Brazil warned it 'will not yield' to such threats.

items.title: UK food inflation could hit 5% next year, BOE warns
items.feedTitle: UK food inflation could hit 5% next year, Bank of England says
items.summary: The Bank of England has warned that UK food price inflation could reach 5% in the coming year as cost pressures mount. The forecast factors in potential energy price cap increases and the lingering effects of regional climate disruptions.

cards.title: Storm Preparedness Reduces Anxiety
cards.insight: Major weather disruptions and power outages reveal that households with basic preparedness plans—water, batteries, non-perishable food, first aid—report significantly lower stress levels during crises. Preparedness shifts control back to individuals, reducing learned helplessness during emergencies.
cards.takeaway: Build a simple 72-hour emergency kit with water, nonperishable food, flashlights, and medications; store it accessibly and review quarterly.

cards.title: Caregiver Burnout Rises with Recognition
cards.insight: While National Family Caregivers Month highlights the contributions of 60+ million American caregivers, research shows that recognition alone without structural support (respite care, employer flexibility, mental health resources) can paradoxically increase burnout by raising expectations without relieving workload.
cards.takeaway: If you are or know a caregiver, prioritize concrete breaks: schedule respite care monthly, set a weekly 'no care' hour, and explore employer caregiver benefits explicitly.

cards.title: Holiday Stress Peaks When Families Avoid Hard Conversations
cards.insight: Data show Americans actually agree on over 100 policy issues, yet politics dominate family tension because avoidance creates anxiety. Naming a conversation's boundaries—topic, time, tone—paradoxically reduces stress and improves connection compared to either forced debate or silent tension.
cards.takeaway: Before holiday gatherings, agree with one person on one difficult topic you'll discuss honestly but briefly; model how to disagree without disconnecting.

cards.title: Post-Holiday Digestive Health Requires Intentional Drainage
cards.insight: Thanksgiving meals leave grease, starch, and fiber buildup in household plumbing and in digestive tracts. Pouring grease down drains causes municipal damage; similarly, skipping hydration and fiber post-holiday slows gastrointestinal recovery. Both require proactive management, not reactionary cleanup.
cards.takeaway: After heavy holiday meals, drink 2–3 liters of water over 24 hours, add soluble fiber (oats, beans), and cool grease in containers before disposal to aid both home and body systems.

ai.summary: A CBS investigation found that Chinese-owned US companies have been purchasing Nvidia's most advanced AI chips, circumventing export restrictions intended to limit Beijing's access to cutting-edge semiconductors. The finding raises questions about enforcement of US technology controls.
